patient_case.prompt_question: A 29-year-old woman comes to the emergency department complaining of painful genital ulcers that have been present for 4 days as well as low-grade fever and malaise. She denies any recent travel, new sexual partners, or antibiotic use. Physical examination reveals multiple clustered vesicles and shallow ulcers in the vulvar region. A Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. Which of the following medications is most appropriate for treating her condition?
patient_case.note: This prompt originates from a clinical scenario; diagnosis or management is to be inferred.

branch.condition: Analyze each option based on known pathophysiology, presentation, and clues
branch.interpretation: Compare each option against clinical findings of herpes simplex virus infection

diagnostic_options.description: Antiviral medication used to treat HSV infections.
evidence_for: Patient's clustered vesicles and shallow ulcers, plus Tzanck smear showing multinucleated giant cells, are consistent with HSV infection.

diagnostic_options.description: Antibiotic primarily used for bacterial infections.
evidence_against: Herpes lesions are viral and not bacterial; antibiotic is ineffective against viruses.

diagnostic_options.description: Antifungal agent used to treat candidiasis.
evidence_against: The clinical findings do not suggest a fungal infection; candida causes thick, white discharge rather than vesicular lesions.

diagnostic_options.description: Antibacterial agent typically used for urinary tract infections and some skin infections.
evidence_against: Not indicated for viral infections such as HSV; does not target the causative agent described.

reasoning_tree.conclusion: Acyclovir is the most appropriate treatment for genital herpes due to its antiviral activity against HSV.
